title: Priority inversion you can reproduce and then bound
objective: Reproduce classic priority inversion with three tasks and a mutex, capture a timeline where High is blocked while Medium runs, then apply a named inheritance or ceiling protocol and show High's blocking time drops to a written bound.
whyThisMatters: A missed deadline that only happens when a low-priority logger holds a lock is the kind of bug plants ship. If you cannot turn inversion on and off in a log, you cannot claim the node is deterministic.
evidence: INVERSION.md naming priority inheritance or priority ceiling and one situation the other protocol would handle differently
A captured timeline (tick log) showing High blocked for at least N ticks while Medium runs and Low still holds the lock, with N written in INVERSION.md
A captured timeline after the fix showing High's blocking time less than or equal to the written bound
Git history with the inversion reproduction committed before the fix
Reflection notes answering the task questions
acceptanceCriteria: The reproduction log shows three named tasks (Low, Medium, High) and a mutex; High is blocked while Medium is running and Low still owns the mutex for at least the N ticks stated in INVERSION.md.
INVERSION.md names exactly one protocol used in the fix: priority inheritance or priority ceiling.
The post-fix log, using the same arrival order, shows High's contiguous blocked time less than or equal to the bound written in INVERSION.md.
INVERSION.md contains one sentence naming a situation the other protocol (the one not implemented) would handle differently.
